title: The word GEOMETRIC is read as the zinc-flake trade name GEOMET: a note about geometric tolerances becomes an exact-text coating reading that "Confirm all read exactly" applies
expected: A note such as "GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES TO ISO 1101." produces no coating reading; the finish question stays as it is without a drawing
actual: finish.coating = "GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES TO ISO 1101." and finish.coatingRoute = zinc_flake, both status 'extracted' (exact text, no needs-checking flag). On a steel cast + machine costing it is a leaning on service.finish, so it is in the "Confirm all read exactly" set; one confirm answers service.finish = zinc_flake and the headless cost moves from £10.1696 to £10.5526 (+3.8 %). On the public NIST CTC-02 sheet five sentences that mention "geometric tolerances" became finish.coating readings and a zinc-flake route, all 'extracted'.
rootCause: server/drawing/extract/coating.ts:12 — the zinc-flake pattern is /\b(?:DACROMET|GEOMET(?:\s?\d{3})?|…)/i with no trailing word boundary, so it matches the start of GEOMETRIC/GEOMETRY. src/engine/engineering-data/interpret-tables.ts:148 has the same problem (/…|geomet|…/i, no boundaries).
recommendedAction: Add a trailing word boundary (GEOMET\b, also for the other trade names) in both tables; add a regression test with the notes "GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES TO ISO 1101", "GEOMETRY" and the NIST CTC-02 sheet; consider marking trade-name-only coating readings needs-validation.

title: A review made on one drawing is replayed onto a different drawing: positional reading ids match a different reading with a different value
expected: Per the design doc, a decision that no longer applies is skipped and listed, never matched to another reading. A review made on real-casting-bracket.pdf (confirming material family = aluminium) must not confirm anything on another drawing.
actual: Sending the bracket's review with the GEAR drawing (via /analyze with that drawing, or /reanalyze naming the gear drawing's hash) applied 'confirm drawing:material.designation:1>material.family' to the gear drawing's reading, whose value is steel (20MnCr5): drawingCosting.answers = {"material.family":"steel"} on the bracket costing. 8 of 10 ops were skipped, 2 applied to different values.
rootCause: Reading ids are positional ("drawing:<parameter>:<n>") and ReviewOp carries neither the drawing hash nor the value that was confirmed (review-state.ts:18-27); replayReview applies any op whose id exists in the new dataset. The screen guards this by resetting the review when the drawing hash changes (src/ui/drawing-review-ui.ts:186-187), but the server accepts any review with any drawing. The same mechanism would apply a stored review to a re-read made by a newer reader version if the reading order changes.
recommendedAction: Stamp each op (or the review) with the drawing hash and reader version and the value seen when the decision was taken; on replay skip an op whose reading's value differs, and refuse/skip a review made for another hash.

title: Core PDF and workbook say "no drawing is read" on a costing that has a drawing read and applied
scenario: D — casting bracket and gear with drawing
expected: With a drawing attached, the DFM 'not checked' line does not claim that no drawing is read
actual: Core PDF §7 (page 8 casting, page 6 gear) and workbook 0-Executive!A235: "Not checked: tolerances, datums and finish call-outs (no drawing is read)." — the same report prints the drawing specification table and the stamp naming the drawing reader.
rootCause: src/export/executive-summary.ts:1342 — the notChecked sentence is a constant written before the drawing reader existed.
recommendedAction: When a drawing is attached, say what the reader does and does not check (e.g. tolerances read but not costed; GD&T symbols drawn as geometry not read).

title: Audit pack §1: the reproducibility stamp runs off the right edge of the page when a drawing is attached
scenario: D — audit pack, casting bracket and gear with drawing
expected: The stamp is printed in full (it is meant to be quoted word for word)
actual: Page 4: "… drawing reader v1.0.0 · real-casting-bracket.pdf 6f1a98cf · 10 Nov 202" (clipped); gear: "… gear-drawing-WRONG-z40.pdf c58b93dd · 10" (date clipped). Without a drawing the line fits.
rootCause: src/export/pdf.ts:1032 — doc.text(`Reproducibility: ${cadMeta.stamp}`, MG, y + 1) with no maxWidth / splitTextToSize; the drawing suffix makes the line wider than the content width.
recommendedAction: Wrap the line (splitTextToSize to CW) and advance y by the wrapped height.

title: PDF drops the thread-depth symbol: "M6x1-6H ↧ 12" prints as "M6x1-6H  12"
expected: The value reads as on the drawing / workbook (M6x1-6H ↧ 12) or with a word ("depth 12")
actual: Audit pack page 22 prints "M6x1-6H  12" (blank where ↧ was); workbook 10-Drawing prints "M6x1-6H ↧ 12". "M6x1-6H 12" can be read as a thread length.
rootCause: src/export/pdf.ts:434 (winAnsiSafe) strips every character outside WinAnsi; U+21A7 has no replacement mapping (Ø, ±, ° and µ survive).
recommendedAction: Map ↧ to "depth" (and ⌴ / ⌵ to "counterbore" / "countersink") in winAnsiSafe before the strip.

title: Two confidence grades for one costing: screen, core PDF and 0-Executive say Medium; audit pack and 1-Summary say Low
scenario: D — all three costings (also with NO drawing)
actual: Casting bracket: screen 'Band · confidence Medium', core PDF p1 'Medium confidence', 0-Executive!A41 'Medium'; audit pack cover 'Model Confidence: Low', executive summary 'CONFIDENCE Low', §7 'Why confidence is Low'; workbook 1-Summary!A24 'Model confidence Low'. Same on both gear costings (with and without drawing).
rootCause: Core grades the DISTINCT inputs (executive-summary.ts:961 gradeOfCounts: 12 inputs, 0 High / 11 Medium / 1 Low → Medium); the audit pack cover / workbook summary grade every data point with overallConfidence(result) (pdf.ts ~2693: 27 points, 0 / 21 / 6 → Low). Not caused by the drawing feature.
recommendedAction: Use one grading function and one input population for every surface; add a test that screen, core, audit and workbook grades are equal.

title: 30 MB exactly: /api/drawing/read refuses it (413) while /api/cad/analyze accepts it
expected: The same limit on both routes (the doc: 'Limit 30 MB')
actual: A 31,457,280-byte PDF: /api/drawing/read → 413 'The drawing is over the 30 MB limit.'; /api/cad/analyze → 200, drawing ready. 30 MB + 1 byte is refused by both.
rootCause: server/routes/drawing.ts:28 sets multer limits.fileSize = MAX_DRAWING_BYTES and busboy fires 'limit' when the size REACHES the limit (node_modules/busboy/lib/types/multipart.js:476 fileSize === fileSizeLimit); cad.ts:805 tests size > MAX_DRAWING_PDF_BYTES.
recommendedAction: Set the multer limit to MAX_DRAWING_BYTES + 1 and check size > MAX in the route, as cad.ts does.

title: Over-limit message rounds the size: "Drawing is 30 MB; the limit is 30 MB."
expected: A message that shows why the file was refused
actual: HTTP 413 'Drawing is 30 MB; the limit is 30 MB.'
recommendedAction: Print one decimal (as server/drawing/ingest.ts checkSize does) or say 'over'.

title: A scan turned 90° is reported as read upright but yields a wrong material (S310N → steel) for an aluminium A356-T6 drawing
expected: The sheet is turned upright before OCR (as a vector PDF with /Rotate is) or the reading says it could not be read reliably
actual: casting-bracket-rot90.png: warning 'the drawing is turned 90° on its page; it was read upright', 52 words at 72 % mean confidence, 3 readings: material.designation 'S310N', material.family 'steel', one dimension. The same sheet upright reads 37 readings incl. A356-T6 / aluminium. All three are needs-validation, so nothing is costed until confirmed.
rootCause: Observed behaviour only; raster/index.ts OCRs the image as given and again after rotate90cw for vertical words (lines 81-121) rather than choosing the page orientation first. Not traced further.
recommendedAction: Detect the page orientation (0/90/180/270) on the whole scan and OCR once in the best orientation; warn when mean confidence is low.

title: Rotation is reported inconsistently: sheet.rotationDeg and the warning disagree
actual: Vector PDF with /Rotate 90: sheets[0].rotationDeg = 90, warning 'the drawing is turned 270° on its page'. Raster turned 90°: rotationDeg = 0, warning 'turned 90°'.
rootCause: rotationDeg is the PDF page /Rotate (pdf-vector.ts:194; raster sheets hard-code 0 at index.ts:150) while the warning prints the dominant text rotation q (index.ts:220-228).
recommendedAction: Report both under distinct names, or report the text rotation in rotationDeg.

title: OCR structural mis-assignments on skewed / low-resolution scans (wrong title-block cells, Ø read as 9, decimal point lost)
expected: Readings that are wrong are absent or flagged; key cells land in the right field
actual: Skew 3°: title.partNumber = 'CASTING BRACKET', title.scale = 'ISO 8062-3 DCTG 6'. Skew 7°: tolerance.general = 'ISO 2768-mK' (the machined-dimension note) instead of DCTG 6. 200 dpi upright: '4× Ø13' read as dimension 913 (×4). 72 dpi: roughness 'Ra 63' (6.3), dimensions 1081 / 122 / 112. Every one is status needs-validation (as documented) and none is confirmed by 'Confirm all read exactly'.
rootCause: Documented OCR limits (doc §5, §9); not traced in code.
recommendedAction: Warn on low resolution (< 150 dpi) and reject title-block values that do not fit their cell (a scale must look like n:m).

title: Server memory after OCR reads: node RSS grows to ~1.1-1.2 GB and stays; peak 2.0 GB (node + geometry worker) on an A0 image
expected: The OCR pass fits the 2 GB VM (doc §3: one at a time because the VM has 2 GB)
actual: Process-group RSS sampled every 150 ms: idle 400-607 MB; A0 300 dpi PNG (14039×9928) read peak 2,019 MB; during the 9-image queue the node process alone was 1,173 MB with the geometry worker at 304 MB; after the run node stayed at 1,104 MB (+2 geometry workers 351 + 349 MB = 1,823 MB group).
rootCause: Not traced; RSS is not returned after the OCR passes (WebAssembly / worker heap). Measured on a 16 GB host, so no OOM was seen.
recommendedAction: Measure in the 2 GB Docker image; cap the OCR image size; terminate the OCR worker after each pass so its memory is returned.

title: Core page 1 says the CAD model shows no thread while the confirmed drawing on the same report states M6x1-6H
expected: With a drawing that states a thread, the 'Not included until answered' item says the drawing states one (not costed)
actual: Page 1: 'Threads not detected — confirm: the CAD model shows no thread … say which holes are tapped and their size'; page 3 lists Thread among the drawing's not-costed readings (M6x1-6H ↧ 12).
recommendedAction: When the drawing states threads, name them in that line.

title: Audit pack §9b heading: the subtitle overlaps the title
scenario: D — casting bracket audit pack page 18
actual: '§9b — Route Comparison' is overprinted by 'the same part on every route and process that can make it in its material · reference: Cast and machine — gravity die casting'. Not seen on the gear (shorter subtitle). Not caused by the drawing feature.
rootCause: Subtitle is right-aligned without a width check against the title.
recommendedAction: Shorten or wrap the subtitle when it would reach the title.

title: DXF reader joins the next note's number to a note and does not read a 'PART No.' text
expected: 'PRESSURE TEST AT 6 bar'; part number CB-2207-11
actual: quality.leakTestSpec = 'PRESSURE TEST AT 6 bar 2.' (the next TEXT's '2.' appended); no title.partNumber from 'PART No. CB-2207-11'. 3 of 6 key readings (material, tolerance, leak, coating found; designation read as EN AC-42100, which is the same alloy).
rootCause: Not traced. The test DXF is hand-made (TEXT entities, no title-block table), so this is indicative.
recommendedAction: Check line assembly for DXF TEXT that starts with a note number.

title: Review cache key includes each decision's timestamp and author
expected: The doc: 'the same decisions give the same text, for cache keys'
actual: reviewStateKey of the same confirm with at 09:00 v 09:05 differs (scripts/keycheck.mts: equal false). Over HTTP (B08) answers and cost were identical; the deterministic /analyze path is never cached, so the key difference only matters on the cached (AI) paths, where a different key means a new model call.
rootCause: review-state.ts:124-130 serialises the whole op including by / at / reason.
recommendedAction: Key on op, id/name and value only; keep by/at for the record.
